join.purpose: Start each task from the project's recorded functional structure, its addresses, purposes and dependents, so inference goes to the task and not to re-orienting in the project.
join.function: Compiles a project's artifacts into namespace types joined by receiver-owned purposes and encounters, and returns the part in scope at the agent's position.
join.relation: orients the agent in the project
join.observation: A semantic compiler records what an artifact is for as typed functional structure.
join.non_goal: Describing code as it is, recalling earlier sessions, or fetching context by embedding distance.

join.purpose: Receive one exact assignment and return an answer that binds to it, whichever session or tool carries the work.
join.function: Issues a durable assignment named by a nonce with its exact prompt and submission header, accepts the answer under that header, and binds a working folder to the assignment.
join.observation: An assignment dispatcher retains the issued prompt and the accepted answer as fixed revisions.

join.purpose: Read its assignment, call module operations and submit answers from inside its own host.
join.function: Exposes assignment, submit, complete, abort, call, status, namespace and resolve as tools keyed by nonce, so one process serves several assignments.
join.relation: gives the agent tool access to its work
join.observation: A tool interface returns each result in one envelope that carries scalars, lists and objects unchanged.

join.purpose: Do the same work from a shell where the working folder decides which module and assignment are in view.
join.function: Presents chassis and module commands as contextual menus with help generated from live contributions, and takes every operation as arguments or as a JSON document from a file or stdin.
join.relation: lets the agent work from a shell
join.observation: A command interface shows only the commands that apply in the current context.

join.purpose: Keep what it learns about one position of the project and read it back at that position in later sessions.
join.function: Stores mutable notes at a namespace address with retained revisions, searchable and updatable through the ordinary operations.
join.observation: An agent memory is local to the namespace position it describes.
join.non_goal: Standing in for the functional record by recalling what happened.

join.purpose: Capture what each artifact is for once, from the artifact itself, so later work starts from that record.
join.function: Issues the canonical intake procedure to an examining agent with access to the artifact and expands its coarse contribution into stored types, elements and joins.
join.observation: An intake turns an artifact into typed functional structure that later operations read.
join.non_goal: Listing every property, purpose or environmental fact of the artifact.

join.purpose: Hold the understanding as one shared record whose addresses stay put when the implementation changes.
join.function: Stores namespace objects under reversible dotted addresses with owned, revisioned joins and exact references, merges imports without rewriting divergent revisions, and keeps referenced bytes immutable.
join.observation: A namespace store keeps each join with the object that owns it.
join.non_goal: Rewriting historical input when current state changes.

join.purpose: Answer why a result is as it is from one reference, through the exact prompt, inputs, run and produced difference.
join.function: Records a production join for every inference or tool result that names the operation, its inputs at their exact revisions and its outputs, and shows that chain from one reference.
join.relation: binds each output to its inputs
join.observation: A provenance recorder keeps the producing occurrence distinct from the content it produced.

join.purpose: Give each agent exactly the knowledge in scope at its position, with the inputs that selected it.
join.function: Applies the mask rule from trunk to leaf, hides results by causal dependency, qualifies properties by branch, and returns the selected sources with the selector and dependency inputs used.
join.observation: A knowledge projector never deletes a stored join to change what is visible.

join.purpose: Produce type-specific knowledge such as best practices or imperatives from one general instruction, kept apart from the structure it describes.
join.function: Runs an authored instruction over each relevant element with its connected purposes and encounters, and attaches each result as an independently versioned layer with its recipe and sources.
join.observation: A layer generator keeps each layer's generations separate from the foundation and from other layers.

join.purpose: Find omissions and other readings of the project from a position outside its implementation.
join.function: Gives an agent that cannot read the repository the complete recorded functional account and receives its agreement, disagreement and omissions as a report.
join.observation: A latent examiner reports on structure and leaves the structure unchanged.
join.non_goal: Turning proposed structure into current elements because a report mentions it.

join.purpose: Change the recorded structure on purpose, with its evidence and reason kept and the earlier revisions left readable.
join.function: Applies an explicit correction, or an inferred expansion of a chosen region, as a new foundation revision.
join.observation: A structure reviser records each change as a new revision beside the one it replaces.

join.purpose: Run intake and every later operation as authored procedures whose meaning stays as written.
join.function: Stores workflow steps and control flow as receiver-owned joins, issues exact prompt snapshots, runs prompt, user, tool, branch, loop, parallel and nested steps durably, and resumes after a restart.
join.observation: A workflow engine keeps each issued prompt and each answer as fixed records.

join.purpose: Keep everything outside the chassis a module that anyone can write, load, disable or remove without disturbing the rest.
join.function: Discovers modules in the System, User and Project places in priority order, activates them in isolation, gives them the public services, and tears them down cleanly while keeping their settings and records.
join.observation: A module runtime isolates one module's failure from the others.

join.purpose: Let the person directing the work see the namespace, edit workflows and run jobs from a browser.
join.function: Serves a browser workbench from one process per data root, with token sign-in, a namespace graph read from one exact snapshot, a workflow editor with inline object references, and record and provenance pages.
join.relation: shows and edits the project's structure
join.observation: A web workbench reads and writes through the same operations as the command line.

join.purpose: Keep each artifact's origin and variants so understanding can be compared with them and the artifact rebuilt without the original repository.
join.function: Captures an origin and its sibling variants as content-addressed payloads, keeps changed text whole below a size threshold and as line edits above it, and reconstructs a chosen version into an empty folder.
join.observation: An artifact archive measures a variant against its origin and never against another variant.

join.purpose: Carry the understanding and the selected modules into hosted agents as one executable file that runs cold and offline.
join.function: Builds an executable wheel holding the chassis, chosen modules with their declared dependencies, project data, retained payloads and pending assignments, tagged for the platforms its native files need.
join.relation: delivers the project to another machine
join.observation: A portable packager takes its dependencies from what each selected module declares.

join.purpose: Keep established semantic terms and the strict typology rules operative and verbatim in every prompt and stored record.
join.function: Defines type identity, the Operative Purpose join roles, the namespace naming rules and the terms that later work may not paraphrase.
join.relation: fixes the meaning of the record
join.observation: A semantic specification names the terms that later work may not rewrite.

join.purpose: Judge completeness against stated outcomes and invariants and not against the implementation's own account of itself.
join.function: Lists numbered outcomes and invariants for the chassis, modules, work identity, provenance, knowledge, workflows, portability and interfaces, and tracks the remediation of each gap.
join.observation: A requirement specification states outcomes and leaves implementation open.

join.purpose: Bring a person or a host agent from first contact to a working install, and a module author to a first module.
join.function: Explains the product in a README, gives host agents a packaged skill and a view of the project's stage, and gives each module a developer README that names its commands and ownership.
join.relation: teaches the system to new users
join.observation: An onboarding guide leads a reader from first contact to a working result.

join.purpose: Give agents working on Metaform itself the same orientation the compiler gives on any project.
join.function: Holds the chassis's own recorded functional account, separate from project knowledge, in the same namespace and joins.
join.observation: A chassis metaform is the recorded functional account of the chassis, kept apart from project records.

join.purpose: Show from outside that the compiler does what its requirements state, and read passing checks against those requirements and not as proof of correctness.
join.function: Runs suites through the public commands, installed and direct-wheel use, cold offline delivery, module removal and shutdown, and repeats them on each push with the executable wheels rebuilt.
join.relation: checks the compiler against its requirements
join.observation: An acceptance verifier observes external behavior and not internal structure.

join.purpose: Run intake as a resumable authored workflow on the same engine that runs every other procedure, so the intake protocol is itself an executable description.
join.function: Executes the canonical intake definition as native workflow steps and takes the examiner's answer under its assignment.
join.observation: An intake workflow can resume after an interruption without repeating retained work.

join.purpose: Instruct the examining agent by the canonical method for finding an artifact's functional structure.
join.function: Gives the target, the choice of a receiving entity outside the artifact, the trace of joins and the naming rules as one authored procedure.
join.observation: An intake procedure states its method and its expected answer shape in one document.

join.purpose: Keep every answer, including one that cannot be read as the requested shape, as a retained object, and join what can be read into the namespace.
join.function: Materializes the coarse contribution as receiver-owned joins beside companion provenance joins, salvages the records that closed in a cut-off answer, and records each mismatch for observation.
join.observation: A namespace store accepts any answer and keeps its source.
join.non_goal: Rejecting the answer or handing it back to the agent.

join.purpose: Know later how far the sources have moved since the intake, so a stale record is seen as stale.
join.function: Captures a hash of each source file at intake and compares the current files with that baseline, reporting added, modified and deleted paths as a percentage.
join.observation: A change reporter compares files without modifying them.

join.purpose: Keep production records as ordinary owned joins that any module can read.
join.function: Commits an outbox with the producer's transaction and publishes universal production joins into namespace storage afterward.
join.observation: A production join names its producing operation, its inputs and its outputs.

join.purpose: Have assigned work carried out by any vendor's agent without changing the assignment.
join.function: Starts a noninteractive Codex or Claude process for an assignment with launch-local tool access, or leaves the assignment for a host agent to answer.
join.relation: hands the assignment to an agent process
join.observation: An assignment can be answered by a process the dispatcher did not start.
join.non_goal: Binding the work to one vendor.

join.purpose: Reach a model through the agent command line the user already has.
join.function: Supplies the noninteractive agent process, its model and its own tool loop.
join.observation: An agent harness hosts the model that answers an assignment.

join.purpose: Identify the work by its nonce and not by the process or client that connects.
join.function: Reads each request's nonce, records the serving process against it, and returns the assignment's prompt, header and enabled operation signatures.
join.observation: A tool interface resolves work from its assignment and never from its client.

join.purpose: Return long work as a durable job that the agent reads later.
join.function: Starts the call in the background and returns a job whose result and event deliveries are read through status.
join.observation: A job keeps its own identity after the client that started it exits.

join.purpose: Begin, submit, complete and abort an assignment from the folder the agent works in.
join.function: Reads the working folder's binding, shows the assignment's prompt and header, and records the submission.
join.observation: A working folder binding names the work in progress and is not part of the artifact.

join.purpose: Read the exact revisions it selects so a result can be reproduced later.
join.function: Resolves selector inputs against retained join revisions at one snapshot.
join.observation: A projection reads and never writes.

join.purpose: Run each generation as an assignment with a receipt so it can be issued again on demand.
join.function: Runs generation through workflow assignments and receipts and records the prompt and inputs that produced each generation.
join.observation: A generation belongs to the layer that requested it.

join.purpose: Address only the elements the instruction applies to, with the knowledge already in scope there.
join.function: Selects the subject elements and their connected purposes, encounters and layers as the instruction's input.
join.observation: A projection returns the sources and inputs behind what it selects.

join.purpose: Ask the affected questions again when a relationship they depended on changes, and leave everything else alone.
join.function: Finds generations whose recorded inputs changed, detaches them, and reissues their producing prompts against the new context.
join.observation: A regeneration replaces an attachment with a new revision and keeps the earlier revisions readable.
join.non_goal: Scheduling reissued work on its own.

join.purpose: Learn which knowledge a changed relationship affects and which prompt produced it.
join.function: Reads each generation's causal inputs and producing operation from production joins.
join.observation: A causal input is a typed reference and not any value that looks like one.

join.purpose: Reason from a position outside the implementation, with no view of the repository.
join.function: Starts a fresh harness process whose tool view is bound to one assignment and serves only the recorded functional context.
join.observation: A fresh harness process carries no memory of the conversation that started it.

join.purpose: Hold the examiner to its outside role.
join.function: Supplies the latent role text and task text that tell it to agree, disagree or report omissions without reading project files.
join.observation: A role prompt states who the agent is for the task and what it must deliver.

join.purpose: Retain the source evidence and the reason for each structural change.
join.function: Attaches the evidence handles and the stated reason to the new revision so the original account and the report stay observable.
join.observation: A structural change never removes the revision it replaces.

join.purpose: Hand a person or an agent the next prompt and wait for its answer without holding a process open.
join.function: Creates an assignment for each prompt step, waits for the sealed answer, and continues from the retained snapshot.
join.observation: A workflow step waits for its answer without holding a process open.

join.purpose: Run tool steps and long steps as work that survives the client and is cancelled truthfully.
join.function: Runs blocking engine work on worker threads inside the operation context and records a cancelled attempt before releasing ownership.
join.observation: A cancelled attempt is recorded as cancelled.

join.purpose: Bind each output to the exact prompt, inputs and attempt that produced it.
join.function: Begins and finishes a production for each tool attempt and retains its consumed inputs and produced outputs.
join.observation: A finished attempt keeps its earlier versions.

join.purpose: Keep each module's settings owned by that module and outside its code.
join.function: Hydrates missing values from the module's declarations without overwriting user values, and keeps values when the module is absent.
join.observation: A setting registry keeps a value a user set apart from the module's default.

join.purpose: Run each module operation in isolation with a settled teardown.
join.function: Executes operations in a persistent local host that outlives the invoking client, and cancels and settles owned work when it stops.
join.observation: A local host owns an accepted invocation to completion.

join.purpose: Let modules cooperate without depending on each other's code.
join.function: Publishes an event to subscribed modules and returns terminal outcomes to a requester.
join.observation: An event bus hands each delivery to a runtime that executes the subscriber.

join.purpose: Show a module's commands, settings and help only where they apply.
join.function: Reads each module's declared commands, settings and help to build contextual menus without importing the module.
join.observation: A module declaration can be read without running its entrypoint.

join.purpose: Let a new author write a module that follows the live contract on the first attempt.
join.function: Provides three teaching modules, a standalone template, an event requester and a harness runner, each with a developer README.
join.observation: A module template runs without any other module installed.

join.purpose: Run each subscriber's handler as attributable work, so a slow or failing handler is reported for that handler and never blocks the publisher or another module.
join.function: Hands each delivery to the runtime, which executes the subscriber and keeps the outcome with the delivery.
join.observation: An event bus does not run workflows of its own.

join.purpose: Keep every revision of a note so a change is never a loss.
join.function: Stores notes as join revisions at the namespace address they describe.
join.observation: A namespace store retains earlier join revisions beside the current one.

join.purpose: Take the artifact's retained bytes with the delivery so the recipient rebuilds it offline.
join.function: Includes the history payloads and registered work-folder contents that the project references.
join.observation: An artifact archive keeps its payloads as immutable content-addressed files.

join.purpose: Ship exactly the modules the recipient needs, with what each declares it depends on.
join.function: Copies the selected module files and their literal dependency declarations into the wheel, and installs them into the recipient's data root on first run while preserving local changes afterward.
join.observation: A module runtime loads a module from any of its places.

join.purpose: Open the chassis configuration and the configured agent commands in the browser, from the same address.
join.function: Runs launcher commands in a pseudo terminal and streams them over a websocket with replay and flow control.
join.observation: A terminal session forwards input, output, control keys and resizes.

join.purpose: Author and run workflows from the browser without a second implementation.
join.function: Shows workflow text with readonly inline object references from the workflow renderer and calls the workflows module's public operations.
join.observation: A workflow engine exposes its operations to any module.

join.purpose: Show the namespace and its joins exactly as stored.
join.function: Projects namespace views from one exact current snapshot and infers no relationship that is not stored.
join.observation: A namespace store keeps each join with the object that owns it.

join.purpose: Keep a terminal alive as a job that the command line and the browser both attach to.
join.function: Submits a chassis job that owns the process and forwards input, output, control keys and resizes.
join.observation: A job keeps its own identity after the client that started it exits.

join.purpose: Judge each requirement by observed behavior and not by the implementation's own claim.
join.function: Enforces each requirement through checks named for it, and labels fixtures and real providers accurately.
join.observation: A requirement specification states outcomes and leaves implementation open.

join.purpose: Prove that the delivered wheel works cold and offline.
join.function: Builds the chassis and teaching-module wheels in continuous integration and runs them from a fresh data root.
join.observation: A portable packager produces one executable file.

join.purpose: Carry the semantic terms unchanged into every intake answer.
join.function: Embeds the core concepts, the namespace rules and their valid and invalid examples in the procedure.
join.observation: A semantic specification names the terms that later work may not rewrite.

join.purpose: Give each runtime role the terms it must not paraphrase.
join.function: Composes each role from shared components for namespace authoring, structural semantics, attachment semantics and aliases.
join.observation: A semantic specification names the terms that later work may not rewrite.

join.purpose: Recognize the exact used device, judge its condition and see how it is used, from the photograph alone, and want to buy it.
join.function: Shows the exact device unchanged as the subject, with its inscriptions and wear legible.
join.relation: shows the device to the buyer
join.observation: A used product photo records the identity and wear of one item.
join.non_goal: Turning the photograph into a schematic, a documentation card or any other kind of visual object.

join.purpose: Place the device where the buyer can see how and where it is used, in light that shows its surface.
join.function: Frames the device inside a scene with its own light, such as a hand holding it against a valley from a trail, where the original shows it on a red fleece blanket.
join.observation: A setting gives the subject a place and a light.

join.purpose: Show the device from an angle that reveals its form, screen and keys instead of a flat overhead view.
join.function: Fixes the camera position relative to the device, as a raised hand-held view in place of the overhead shot of the original.
join.observation: A vantage decides which faces of the subject are visible.

join.purpose: Let the buyer judge the device's size and distance.
join.function: Supplies scale references and layers of foreground and background, such as a hand and a distant valley, where the original has neither.
join.observation: A depth cue lets a viewer read the size of a subject.

join.purpose: Keep the small markings that identify the device readable.
join.function: Renders the brand name, the module labels and the antenna band number sharply enough to read, where the original cuts the band number at the frame edge and blurs the small print.
join.observation: An inscription identifies an item only while it can be read.

join.purpose: Draw the buyer's eye to the device and its key features first.
join.function: Uses framing, focus and light so the device is the sharpest and best lit thing in the frame.
join.observation: An attention cue ranks the parts of a frame by how soon a viewer sees them.

join.purpose: Show the device at a moment that tells the buyer what it does.
join.function: Captures the device in use, with a message on its screen and a hand on its keys, where the original shows only the start-up logo.
join.observation: A captured moment decides what a still image can tell about use.

join.purpose: Take on a defined role and carry out its staged work to a stated deliverable without deviating from the specification.
join.function: States the role, its phases, its allowed tools and the checks that gate each hand-off.
join.observation: A prompt tells an agent who it is for the task and what it must deliver.

join.purpose: Split a task among analyst, planner, implementer, tester and verifier roles that each hand off a defined artifact.
join.function: Orders the roles into a pipeline in which a strict evaluator blocks progression until defects are gone.
join.observation: A pipeline prompt names each role's input and output.

join.purpose: Produce new role prompts for a requested use instead of writing each by hand.
join.function: Analyzes the request, designs the roles and their verification, and writes the resulting prompt.
join.observation: A generator prompt takes a request and returns a prompt.

join.purpose: Put a Metaform expert on a chosen task, from feature discovery to specification, review or README work.
join.function: Carries Metaform's foundation together with one specialist's methods and deliverable in a single role.
join.observation: A specialist prompt combines domain knowledge with one role's method.

join.purpose: Give the Metaform experts the same semantic foundation, unchanged.
join.function: Carries the MetaformFoundation block verbatim in the prompts that commission expert work on the platform.
join.observation: A semantic specification names the terms that later work may not rewrite.

join.purpose: Become bundled workflows the platform can run instead of prompts pasted by hand.
join.function: Imports an authored document with its wording and aliases retained, and infers executable steps in a separate preparation assignment.
join.observation: A workflow import never executes what it imports.
